severity_scale.critical: can silently give a wrong pass/feasible verdict, touch hardware outside the owner steps, or lose data undetected
severity_scale.high: wrong verdict in a realistic case, a gate vacuous or impossible by construction, leakage, a seam that stops the pipeline, or an owner step that blocks
severity_scale.medium: misleading output or failure handling, a surviving mutant on gate logic, a schema mismatch a consumer will misread

status_meaning.confirmed: an independent verifier re-ran a reproduction and saw the defect
status_meaning.plausible: upheld by verifiers on file:line evidence but not reproduced by them

findings.title: The rung 3 identity gate counts crossing windows with no labelled observation as passed trials, so a scored run passes on one real crossing and nineteen empty windows.
findings.failure_scenario: A truth.jsonl whose windows hold no labelled observation counts each such window as a passed trial (n = len(rows); windows_met n >= 20; failed only counts silent swaps). This happens when every frame in a window is marked '?' (the hardest overlaps), when window times are on another clock than the frame times, or when windows fall after the take ends. A scored run then prints 'gate: PASSED' with exit 0 and a 13.9% bound, built from a single real crossing.
findings.reproduction: python3 scratchpad/probes/R3/probe_r3a_vacuous_windows.py <checkout>. Baseline (1 real window): exit 1, 'gate: NOT MET (fewer than 20 windows)'. Variant A (19 windows after the take): 'exit 0; windows 20, windows with 0 observations 19, gate passed True, bound 0.1391'; CLI: 'gate: PASSED'. Variant B: 4 windows whose frames are all '?' are each counted as a trial with 0 scored observations.
findings.suggested_fix: Admit a window only if it holds scored observations of at least two people (or the owner-declared people), and report the rest as excluded. Gate on admitted windows, and refuse when admitted windows fall short of the plan.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: Variant B (all-'?' windows) did not reach PASSED in the reporter's run: 5 windows, gate False. It only shows the counting. A realistic way to get empty windows: the owner marks a crossing they can see in the video, but the detector produced no observations during it (low light, a stall, or a recording cut short). A failure of the tracker or detector is then counted as a passed trial and pushes n up to the 20-window minimum. A clock mismatch on every window does NOT pass, because pooled IDF1 becomes None and idf1_met is False. | The verdict holds. Some trigger wording is weak. A '?' on every frame of a crossing window several seconds long is unrealistic; the probe only got it with 0.02 s windows. A clock mismatch on every take fails safe: pooled IDF1 becomes None and the gate is NOT MET. The mismatch has to hit only some takes. The realistic triggers are: truth files whose window lines exist with no in-window frame labels (unfinished or autosaved labelling), a mistyped epoch window time, or a capture gap during a take. Silent swaps are not hidden: switches are found across the whole take, and a silent one outside windows still fails the gate. Only n is inflated (windows_met and the bound). The one visible hint is IDF1 'n/a' in the per-window table rows; there is no warning or problem line. Fix as suggested: admit only windows that hold scored observations of the take's people, and report the excluded ones.
findings.rank_reason: wrong verdict: scored gate passes on windows with no evidence

findings.title: Under per-light-class scope the rung 7 gate pools held-out coverage across classes, so a class scale with no independent or later-day check passes as measured and anchored.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner chooses k_L_scope = per-illuminant-class (a named option of the pending photometry-commissioning decision). coverage() collects held_out from every group into one list (card.py:416-424), and the days, points and daylight requirements are checked on that pooled list. Line 425 only requires that each group has a fit; it never requires that each group has a held-out point or a held-out day. Example: bulbs is fully checked and daylight has one check, while one 'mixed' capture at counter-1 becomes the mixed group's fit with nothing held out, its meter reading 30% off the bulbs scale. The score prints RUNG 7 GATE: PASS. room_model.jsonl writes status measured with k_L_by_illuminant.mixed = 0.13. The mixed CalibrationRecord says checks.held_out.result = pass with 0 points in it (k_L_records copies the global held_out result, card.py:537). The mixed LightState is anchored at 136.1 lx. Second case: every class has only same-day held-out points, so no k_L is checked on a later day, and the gate still passes. The same data under single scope fails.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/R7/probe_per_class_unchecked_kl.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-7-photometry -> 'RESULT gate=pass held_out=pass missing=[]', 'RESULT group=mixed fit=20261112-7 k_L=0.130000 held_out_points=0', 'RESULT room photometric status=measured k_L_by_illuminant={bulbs: 0.1, daylight: 0.12, mixed: 0.13}', 'RESULT record cal-den-oak-kL-1-mixed: checks.held_out.result=pass n_points(global)=4 points_in_this_record=0', 'RESULT mixed LightState anchored=True value=136.136 lx', 'FAIL scenario 2: gate PASS although no k_L was checked on any day but its own fit day', 'RESULT control single scope: gate=fail'; exit 1
findings.suggested_fix: Compute coverage per group: each group needs its own held-out points spanning min_days, the required points and (where applicable) daylight. A group without them makes the gate incomplete, and its record carries its own held-out result.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: None of substance. Note that the summary does print 'k_L [mixed]: ...' with no held-out lines under it, so an attentive reader could notice. Nothing warns, though: the gate, CalibrationRecord, RoomModel and LightState all claim pass, measured and anchored. | Scenario 1 depends on reading METHOD's coverage rule per group. Under an "any group" reading, METHOD's own text would also pass it. Scenario 2 contradicts METHOD under either reading, and it is exactly what README step 8's minimal two-day flow produces under per-class scope. That makes the realistic case stronger than the finding states: following the README, no class's k_L is ever checked on a later day, yet the gate passes and the LightStates are anchored. Severity stays critical, contingent on the owner choosing per-illuminant-class.
findings.rank_reason: wrong verdict: an unchecked light class is qualified as measured

findings.title: The rung 10 verifier drops misses but keeps hits at points touched by a held light, even at a small light share, so a failing session is reported as a pass.
findings.failure_scenario: A person dims one den bulb, and den_lighting holds it until 120 s of vacancy. While the hold is in force, a scene change is verified. With four ceiling bulbs, the held bulb gives at least 5% (held_share_min, proposed) of the light at every point. evaluate() sets excluded_held only when status == 'outside' (line 303), and run() (lines 576-583) counts every within row as a hit. So for that decision only hits can count. One decision with 3 of 20 points within reports hits=3 misses=0, value 1.0, verdict pass. A run of two free decisions at 16/20 plus two held decisions at 16/20 reports 64/72 = 0.889 pass, while the unheld evidence is 32/40 = 0.80 fail. VERIFY-V1.md's 'see owner questions' for this choice points to a section that does not exist.
findings.reproduction: python3 probes/R10/probe_atk-held-hits-kept-misses-dropped.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-10-verify -> 'held bulb share ... 0.123'; 'RESULT case1 held, 3 of 20 within: tool hits=3 misses=0 value=1.0 verdict=pass excluded_held=17'; 'RESULT case2 control not held ...: hits=3 misses=17 value=0.15 verdict=fail'; 'RESULT case3 mix: tool hits=64 misses=8 value=0.8889 verdict=pass'; 'FAIL: ...'. Mutant 'held-symmetric-exclusion' survives the suite, so no test pins this choice.
findings.suggested_fix: Leave points at or above held_share_min out of both hits and misses: set excluded_held regardless of status, and report them separately. Or make this an open slot / owner decision with both options built.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: The asymmetric choice is written down (VERIFY-V1.md:80). It is not an undocumented accident. It was never put to the owner as a slot or option, though: the 'see owner questions' reference points at nothing. report.json does give excluded_held_or_superseded. The console verdict line and hit_rate.verdict carry no warning. Line refs are correct: score.py:303, plus score.py:576-583. | Severity high, not critical. The asymmetry is stated in VERIFY-V1.md and follows the ladder's literal wording. The report's excluded_held_or_superseded count equals the number of misses dropped (only outside points are excluded), so the conservative rate hits/(hits+misses+excluded) can be recovered from the report. Still a wrong verdict in a realistic scenario (any decision verified while a hold is in force). Add to the scenario: Decision.verify.within_tolerance is written true for such decisions, and that is a field downstream attribution reads. The suggested fix stands. Because the ladder wording is ambiguous, building both options as a named choice for the owner matches the spec README.
findings.rank_reason: wrong verdict: misses near held lights are dropped and a failing session passes

findings.title: The rung 8 probe restore retry writes over a bulb that a person changed by hand during the restore, against the rule that a person's change is never written again.
findings.failure_scenario: A walks in at step 4 (occupancy abort). The tool restores. During the hold-check wait, A sets light.den_rear_right by hand to 37/3100 K. den_lighting records A's hold; the check reports den_rear_right as a failed restore; attempt 2 sends light.turn_on 200/4000 K to it and overwrites A's setting. session.json says restored with unrestored [], and the tool prints 'Every bulb was restored and den_lighting resumed.' restore(), wait_state() and settle_holds() never run guard.classify, so attempt 1 also writes any bulb a person changed after the last guard read.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/R8s1/probe_restore_overwrites_person.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-8-stage1 -> RESULT tool REST writes to that bulb after the person's change: [('turn_on', {'entity_id': 'light.den_rear_right', 'transition': 0, 'brightness': 200, 'color_temp_kelvin': 4000})]; hold checks [(1, ['light.den_rear_right']), (2, [])]; unrestored []; bulb now on 200/4000; FAIL
findings.suggested_fix: Before every restore write, and before attempt 2, compare a fresh HA read with the last one using guard.classify. A bulb changed with a foreign context goes to owner.foreign and is listed as unrestored, never written.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: The reporter's probe passes about 6 runs in 7, because the change usually lands inside den_lighting's 3 s attribution window after the tool's write. With the proposed slots (hold_check_wait_s 5, settle_limit_s 5), a hand change more than 3 s after the bulb's last restore write (the end of the wait, or during settle_holds) becomes a hold, and attempt 2 then overwrites it. For attempt 1, PLAN 'Limits' accepts a fraction-of-a-second gap between re-read and write. But finish()'s re-read never classifies, and the real gap runs from the abort's guard read through the camera release, frame deletion and other bulbs' wait_on (up to settle_limit_s). Deterministic repro: verify_restore-overwrites-person-change.py. | The reporter's probe is timing-dependent: in the fake, a physical-switch-style change that lands within den_lighting's 3 s learn window of the tool's own restore write is never learned. In that case the tool makes no new write, but resume_automatic plus den_lighting still put the bulb back at the snapshot, so A's setting is lost either way. For a deterministic reproduction use probes/R8s1/probe_restore_overwrites_person_change_svc.py, where A's change is an HA service call.
findings.rank_reason: hardware: rewrites a bulb a person set by hand

findings.title: With the proposed read-frame background, perfectly executed offs and deep dims score as misses in the rung 10 verifier and can flip the gate to fail.
findings.failure_scenario: D = measured_ref - E(before) (score.py:274) puts the light model's error at the brighter before-state into the 'daylight' term. That error is then judged at ±15% of a much smaller after-state prediction, with no floor and no uncertainty term (score.py:286-290). Setup: the model is 5% off at the before state (rung 8's own target is a median of 8%) and every bulb lands as commanded. A vacancy OFF then gives predicted = D, so points with D > 0 read -97% (outside) and points with D <= 0 are unverifiable: the result depends on the sign of the model error. A dim-down 0.8->0.1 reads -23% and +49% at every point. Three on-scenes that pass alone (18/18) become 18/27 = 0.667 'fail'. Off and dim scenes are routine for the incumbent the ladder asks rung 10 to verify.
findings.reproduction: python3 probes/R10/probe_dark-scene-false-misses.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-10-verify -> 'RESULT d-off: [(p0, outside, -0.9655), (p1, unverifiable, None), ...]'; 'RESULT d-dim: [(p0, outside, -0.2294), (p1, outside, 0.4902), ...] causes unexplained'; 'RESULT tool with dark scenes: hits 18 misses 9 value 0.6667 -> fail'; 'RESULT tool without them: hits 18 misses 0 value 1.0 -> pass'; 'FAIL ...'
findings.suggested_fix: Add an open slot for a minimum predicted level (below it a point is unverifiable), and use the fixed uncertainty bounds in the point check as the increments already do. Or estimate D only from points whose before-state light is small relative to the measurement.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: Narrow the scenario. A moderate dim (up to about 3:1 at 5-8% model error) does not flip. Only a deep dim or OFF flips it, and an OFF only counts if the off decision carries verify points; a vacancy-off with no targets may have none. The result is a false fail, not a false pass. It occurs under the proposed 'reference_frame' background only, not under 'zero'. | The probe's model error is a per-point scale error at every state, not only 'at the before state'. The fully dark case is avoided by the documented 'zero' background; the defect remains for the proposed default after dark and for any twilight run. The wrong verdicts point toward fail, which is conservative but still a wrong verdict in a realistic scenario, so high stands.
findings.rank_reason: wrong verdict: correctly executed dark scenes fail the gate

findings.title: The rung 5 gate reports pass, scored runs included, when its clauses check nothing: empty inputs, crossings that match no track, or no crossings file at all.
findings.failure_scenario: The verdict is 'fail' only when some clause recorded a failure (gate.py:170). Nothing requires that anything was checked. (a) An empty bundles file and an empty requests file with one annotated crossing give verdict pass, exit 0. (b) The tracker stays confident through the crossing, so every bundle meeting it has association_safe true. The crossings file gives the interval as [5.0, 7.0], which is relative seconds, the form every CLI time argument accepts, or it names track ids the tracker does not use. The crossing clause checks 0 bundles and the verdict is pass, exit 0. The same bundles with Unix times exit 1. (c) Track lines whose last_obs_ids name no observation in the file (for example an observation file from another run) are silently dropped as undated: records.py:100 counts them and den_bundle.py never reports the count. route then sends nothing and prints only its practice line, and the gate passes. (d) With every slot closed in temp copies of METHOD-V1.md and ROUTER-V0.md, `gate --scored` on an empty bundles file with no --requests and no --crossings prints 'verdict: pass' with no practice note and exits 0. Every clause shows 'checked 0', and the router clauses are not listed at all.
findings.reproduction: python3 probes/R5/probe_gate_vacuous_pass.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-5-bundle -> 'FAIL (a) empty bundles + empty requests + 1 crossing: exit 0, verdict: pass (practice: ...)'; 'FAIL (b) confident tracker, crossing written [5.0, 7.0]: exit 0, [crossing ok checked 0] | verdict: pass ... ; same bundles with Unix-time crossing: exit 1, verdict: fail'; 'FAIL (c) 142 track lines, none dated: route printed "practice replay with a fake sender: ..."; gate exit 0, verdict: pass'; 'FAIL (d) --scored, slots closed, empty bundles, no requests, no crossings: exit 0, verdict: pass'; 'RESULT FAIL: 4 of 4 empty or unmatched inputs got verdict pass'
findings.suggested_fix: Fail or refuse (exit 2) when there are no bundles, when any clause checked 0, or when an annotated crossing is met by no bundle of each track it names. Make --scored require --requests and --crossings, and refuse when Store.undated > 0.
findings.verification: 3 report(s) merged; 6 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: The severity stays high, not critical, because the per-clause 'checked 0' counts are visible. The strongest realistic case is a crossing whose track_ids name tracks the tracker does not use (A/B against T1/T2), more than relative times. | None of substance. The 'checked 0' counts are printed, so the pass is not fully silent, which keeps this at high rather than critical. The cited lines (gate.py:170, records.py:100) are correct.
findings.rank_reason: wrong verdict: scored gate passes when nothing was checked

findings.title: Rung 3 lets the same held-out takes be re-scored after a tracker retune under an unchanged method fingerprint and version, and overwrites the earlier report, so the leak leaves no trace.
findings.failure_scenario: After a failed E2 score, a builder changes tracker_core.py (a diagnosis-informed retune) without touching METHOD.md, and the owner reruns track and score on the same held-out takes. The fingerprint (method.py:76-78, METHOD block only) is unchanged. tracks.run.json (pipeline.py:85-95) records neither a code version nor a tracks.jsonl hash, so score_session (162-169) accepts the new tracks. The report claims the same method version and fingerprint, and den_track.py:138 overwrites the earlier e2-report.json, so no trace remains. The README (166-167) and the ladder require fresh takes after diagnosis-informed tuning. Hand-edited tracks.jsonl files are also accepted.
findings.reproduction: S=$SCRATCH; python3 -B $S/probes/R3/probe_r3v_fingerprint_ignores_code_and_tracks.py $S/wt/rung-3-track (works on a temp copy) -> 'RESULT before code change: exit 1, SCORED, fingerprint sha256:ece92698d5d151bb, silent 0, reported 22, ambiguous share 0.465' / 'RESULT after code change : exit 1, SCORED, fingerprint sha256:ece92698d5d151bb, silent 13, reported 9, ambiguous share 0.149, problems []' / 'RESULT after editing 5 records of touching_crossing-0-typical/tracks.jsonl: exit 1, problems []' / 'FAIL count: 2'.
findings.suggested_fix: Fingerprint the tool's source files (or the git commit plus a dirty flag) together with the METHOD block. Store sha256 of tracks.jsonl in tracks.run.json and verify both at score time. Write each scored report to a new file and refuse to re-score takes already scored under another fingerprint.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: Kept high, with these qualifications. The leak needs someone to re-score the same takes after a retune, which README.md:166-167 and METHOD.md:255-258 forbid. Still, 're-run track and score to see if the fix worked' is the natural next step. The tool labels that run SCORED with the same version and fingerprint and overwrites the failed report, so the leak cannot be detected afterwards. The hole is wider than the finding says: nothing records which takes were already scored, so re-tracking old takes after a proper METHOD.md version bump is accepted too. Fingerprinting the code alone would not close it; the run needs a record of takes already used. The hand-edited tracks.jsonl part is an adversarial case and would be low on its own. | None to the facts. The probe shows the same takes re-score under an unchanged fingerprint with a different result. It does not show a fail flipping to a pass; both runs exit 1. The leak still needs someone to re-run on takes already scored, but the tool's only guard against that misses code changes and keeps no record of the earlier report.
findings.rank_reason: wrong verdict: held-out takes re-scored after tuning with no trace

findings.title: Correction capture counts the gap between two non-overlapping recorder exports as occupied hours, which can flip its budget verdict.
findings.failure_scenario: The README (lines 149-151) tells the owner to add later exports to extend the window. Suppose the owner exports on 11-07, again on 11-19, and the recorder has purged the days between. If export 1's last status row shows automatic + occupancy on (the owner exporting from the den PC), walk() adds the whole span from that row to export 2's first row as in-charge exposure (_add at line 315). There is no overlap check and no warning; the revision went up, so no restart is seen. Holds already present in export 2's first row would also be counted as new corrections instead of held_at_export_start. Result: 12 real occupied hours become 294, the min_occupied_h gate is passed by time nobody saw, and the verdict reads beyond_budget instead of insufficient.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/R0corr/probe_export_gap_counted_as_exposure.py $SCRATCH/wt/correction-capture -> 'RESULT export 1 alone: occupied_h=6.0 people=2 verdict=insufficient' / 'RESULT exports 1+2 (gap 12 days): occupied_h=294.0 people=4 per_h=0.0136 verdict=beyond_budget restarts=0' / 'FAIL the 12-day gap between exports is counted as 282.0 occupied hours'
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a file boundary like a restart: no exposure across it, and holds in the next file's first row count as held_at_export_start. Or refuse unless each later export starts at or before the previous one's last row.
findings.verification: 1 report(s) merged; 2 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: Secondary claim, refined: a hold that began inside the gap and shows in export 2's first row is counted as a new 'opened' correction in every_hold, normally with source 'unknown' (my probe: counted=[(True, 'unknown', 'opened')]). It is not counted as a person unless a bulb row falls within 5 s. It is not held_at_export_start. The 282 h figure comes from the probe's two lone evenings; a realistic purge gap adds tens of hours (47 h here), which is still enough to flip the verdict. | The magnitude is wrong for the finding's own dates. With 10-day retention, exports on 11-07 and 11-19 leave a gap of about 2 days (about 49 h counted), not 12 days. A 12-day gap means exports about 22 days apart. The defect and the high severity stand. The verdict is a planning value, and the inflated hours mostly push it toward beyond_budget or turn insufficient into a verdict. The suggested fix (treat a file boundary like a restart, or refuse exports that do not overlap) is sound.
findings.rank_reason: wrong verdict: unseen hours flip the planning verdict

findings.title: The rung 1 mount check reports the camera unchanged after small turns or slides that move registered points by 5 to 40 cm, so the stale registration stays valid.
findings.failure_scenario: The camera is bumped 5 degrees in yaw. check-mount compares the 8x8 per-cell median depths using the proposed 50 mm / 3% / more-than-half-of-cells values. Only 27 of 64 cells change, so it prints MOUNT UNCHANGED, and the README says that keeps the registration. Meanwhile the old transform misplaces points in the working region by 22 to 40 cm. A 1 degree pitch (4.7 to 8.7 cm off) and an 8 cm slide along a wall (8 cm off) also read 'unchanged'. A floor's depth image does not change when a level camera turns about the vertical axis, so tightening the slots helps only through walls and furniture, and depth noise limits how tight they can go. Every later Observation keeps resolving to the stale transform as valid.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/R1/probe_mount-check-blind-to-yaw.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-1-register -> 'FAIL yaw 5.0 deg check-mount unchanged (27 of 64 cells changed); old registration off by: room centre 1.0 m up 21.7 cm, seat 0.5 m up 31.6 cm, far floor 40.3 cm' ... 'RESULT FAIL: 6 motions break the 5 cm gate while check-mount says unchanged'. The probe calls the tool's own scene.mount_signature and scene.check_mount. Mutants that require 95% of cells or multiply the tolerance by 4 survive the suite (mutate_den-register.py rows 8 and 9), because the only moved-camera test shifts the whole background by 70 cm (test_den_register.py:560).
findings.suggested_fix: Do not let 'unchanged' confirm a registration. Re-verify by re-clicking the marks (at least the checks) on a new frame against the 5 cm gate, or compare the left-image positions of the marks with a pixel threshold derived from 5 cm at their range.
findings.verification: 1 report(s) merged; 2 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: The defect occurs with the proposed values of four slots that are still open. In my noise-free cluttered scene, tighter values (20 mm / 1% / 0.25) did flag yaw 2 deg, yaw 5 deg and the 8 cm slide, and an unmoved camera stayed 'unchanged'. So 'tightening helps only through walls and furniture' is true, but walls and furniture are enough for tighter slots to work in synthetic data. Whether tighter values survive real depth noise and people in view was not tested. Yaw 1 deg (4.3 cm at the room centre, about 8 cm at the far floor) was caught only at 10 mm / 0.5% / 0.1. The decision line is scene.py:233; the overclaim is at register.py:515-517 and README.md:149. | Severity stays high. The claim is real at even smaller motions than the headline: a 1 degree yaw or pitch already breaks 5 cm at far points while only 1-2 of 64 cells change.
findings.rank_reason: wrong verdict: a moved camera is reported unchanged

findings.title: The rung 3 reader merges a box-only and a keypoint observation of two different people during a crossing, so one track lists the other person's observation.
findings.failure_scenario: den-observe (observe.py, detections.from_perception_lab) writes one observation per detector box: keypoints (rtmpose-m) when the box got a pose, else person_box (yolo26s). It never writes two observations of one person, which is what synth.py writes and what _merge assumes. In a crossing, the occluded person's low-score box often gets no pose. Its box overlaps the front person's box by IoU >= 0.5, the models differ, and _merge makes one measurement. B's track lists A's observation in last_obs_ids, A's own track misses and coasts (it would end after 4 s), and the scorer counts phantom switches. Downstream, den-bundle's person_frames lets a person_box win a tie, so B's bundle would crop A.
findings.reproduction: python3 scratchpad/probes/R3/probe_r3a_merge_two_people.py <checkout>, with records shaped as den-observe writes them. Output: 'frames where A is box-only behind B: 5; measurements merged from two observations: 5'; 't=3.50 T1 ambiguous last_obs_ids=[...-0, ...-1] (persons [A, B])' x5; "A's own track T2 while A is detected behind B: ['coasting', 'confirmed']"; 'switches in window 10 (silent 0, reported 10), IDF1 0.853'. RESULT FAIL. Code: rung-2-observe tools/den-observe/observe.py observe(), one observation per detection.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not merge across observations from one detector row. Merge only when the producer marks two observations as the same detection, or drop the merge for den-observe's format and test against fixtures written from its record shape.
findings.verification: 1 report(s) merged; 2 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: Phantom switches are scored as reported (ambiguous), not silent. The E2 effect is lower IDF1, so a false NOT MET is likely, plus A's track coasting while A is detected. Two people seated close with overlapping boxes would keep A's track coasting and ending in live use. The merge can be correct for near-duplicate boxes of one person that survive NMS. The downstream den-bundle tie claim was not checked in this verification. | Mitigating facts: the _merge docstring admits pairings can be wrong when people overlap, and the builder followed the spec rule to test from schemas.json fixtures. Track.last_obs_ids ('keypoints included') allows a box plus keypoints per person, so this is a seam defect between rungs 2 and 3, not a contract breach by either alone. On E2 it errs toward a false FAIL: phantom switches, silent ones once A's own track has ended, and lower IDF1. It needs both overlapping boxes to come out of the detector at IoU >= 0.5; an NMS at IoU 0.7 would drop some of them. High stands, because the merge never helps on den-observe's format and gives a wrong verdict in plausible near-pass or along-view takes.
findings.rank_reason: wrong verdict: two people merged into one observation on real data

findings.title: An error reply from the home system mid-session makes the rung 8 probe skip restore and resume and print that nothing changed, while the incumbent stays paused and bulbs stay lit.
findings.failure_scenario: During a session, HA answers one light.turn_on or turn_off with a non-200 reply. Real HA answers 500 when an integration raises, for example when the Hue bridge is briefly unreachable; 401 if the token is revoked. HA.request raises sweep.Refused (probe.py:86-87). Session.send, apply, probe, finish and abort catch only HAUnreachable and Abort, so the Refused escapes Session.run, and main prints 'Refused: ... This command changed nothing.' with exit 2 (probe.py:939-941). The README says exit 2 means nothing was changed. In fact den_lighting is left paused, a bulb is left at a probe level, the camera hold is never released (it times out), session.json stays at phase 'probing', and the message never mentions --recover. The owner believes nothing happened, so the den lights stop following occupancy until someone notices. The same escape happens in the restore and resume path, for example when the switch turn_on is refused after an abort.
findings.reproduction: python3 -I probes/R8s1/probe_ha_error_reply_mid_session.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-8-stage1 -> RESULT exit=2 stderr='Refused: Home Assistant answered 400 to POST /api/services/light/turn_off. This command changed nothing.'; RESULT session.json phase='probing' outcome='probing' restore=None resume=None; RESULT den_lighting automatic switch='off'; bulbs left on=['light.den_front_left']; camera still held=True; 2 FAIL
findings.suggested_fix: Once the session has paused den_lighting, turn any non-200 from HA into Abort (ha_lost-style: stop, keep paused, tell the owner to run --recover), and never print 'changed nothing' after the pause.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: The defect is real, but the triggers the finding cites do not reach this path on real HA. A 500 from a raising integration (for example the Hue bridge unreachable) and a 401 for a revoked token come back with aiohttp's plain-text bodies ('500 Internal Server Error...', '401: Unauthorized'). request() turns those into HAUnreachable('reply is not JSON'), so the session aborts as ha_lost, keeps den_lighting paused and tells the owner to run --recover. That is correct handling, and the switch.turn_on-refused-after-abort example is handled the same way. The path is reached only by a non-200 reply whose body is empty or JSON. On real HA that is mainly the empty-body 503 HA sends while stopping (an HA restart during the session), which I reproduced end to end. The fake HA's JSON error bodies (synthetic.py:440-446, 492-493) do not match real HA, which hid the distinction. Because the trigger is narrow and session.json stays at 'probing' (so --recover works once the owner knows to run it), this is misleading failure handling: medium, not high. The suggested fix still applies: after the pause, treat any non-200 as an ha_lost-style Abort. | The failure scenario's own example is wrong. When an integration raises, real HA answers 500 with an aiohttp plain-text body (HTTPBadRequest/401 replies are plain text too), and probe.py turns that into HAUnreachable('reply is not JSON'), which is the correct ha_lost abort. The reporter's fake replies 400 with a JSON body, which real HA does not send
findings.rank_reason: hardware: session left paused with bulbs lit and a false message

findings.title: On a model the size of rung 8's grid, rung 9 decision records exceed the 16 KB line limit, so a scored run aborts and writes no log.
findings.failure_scenario: Scored run with rung 8's 32x18 = 576-block model and compensation P1 (the gate's proposed option). Each rejected candidate's why string lists every broken (bulb, point) pair (decide.py:339). Each held bulb's footprint lists point ids across all model points (decide.py:249-257). recipients carry one row per (track, task point) for every lit channel (decide.py:536-545). A single Decision line is 229-472 KB, and runner.run's events.validate (events.py:86) raises 'decision line over 16384 bytes'. run.py exits 'run.py: decision line over 16384 bytes' with no log, so there is nothing to score. none-v0 overflows the same way at 32 or more task points on the one 'room' track.

The suite misses this because holds.run_case and TimingTest call decide.handle directly and never validate.
findings.suggested_fix: Summarise rejected candidates and footprints (counts, a few example points, or a hash with detail in a side file), and keep recipients per track rather than per block. Add a test that pushes full-size-model Decisions through runner.run.
findings.verification: 1 report(s) merged; 2 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: Most of the P1 bloat is the rejected candidates' why strings, not the recipients. Under the proposed compensation_form 'mode', decide.py:286-287 lifts the bound only for trigger 'mode change'. So the oversize lines come from 'person_state change' and 'hold change' decisions taken while a bulb is held, and those are common during reading. The path is reachable only once a full-size real model can be loaded (see atk-stage1-model-refused), but it then blocks every P1 scored run that has a hold. | Severity high is right: under the gate's proposed option P1, a scored run is impossible on any rung-8-sized model. The 16384 limit is enforced only in events.py; README's den-event-1 section never states it. Under none-v0 the threshold is about 25 task points on 'room'. findings.title: Rung 5 replay admits detector results by capture time and ignores rung 2's arrival time, so replayed bundles hold evidence that had not arrived when they were sent.
findings.failure_scenario: Track lines are dated by the capture_ts they name (records.py:94). Frames, keypoints and object boxes are admitted by capture_ts alone (assemble.py:71-89, 131). METHOD-V1.md:39 says 'only records known by t1 are read: observations captured by then'. Rung 2 (den-observe ab491a88) writes freshness.available_ts on every Observation, and note R5 puts capture-to-completion at about 1.46 s. In a replay at 1.46 s latency with a result every 0.5 s, every routed bundle holds 3 of 7 keypoint entries and 3 of 7 frames that arrived after its send. Its crop_ref is cut from a frame that had not arrived. At 1.6 s latency the causal bundle flags track, person_box and keypoints as stale; the tool flags nothing. On den-observe's own demo output (0.3 s latency), a bundle at the last capture holds 2 of 6 entries not yet available. The gate checks with the same capture-time view and passes all of these. The contracts leave the arrival field open: schemas.json Observation has no arrival time, and den-observe slots it as freshness_field. By the builder rules it should therefore be an open slot that blocks scored runs; here it is neither slotted nor raised as an owner question. Effect: the ladder's rung 5 checkpoint (N2's frozen gate re-run with causal routing) would be fed bundles a live router could not build. Example: at the 4 s pace with a 1.25 s service time, the worst-case delay from an event to an answer is 5.25 s for one person and 9.25 s for two in this replay, inside owner-choices' 6 s / ~10 s detection grace. Once 1.46 s of detector latency is counted it is 6.71 s / 10.71 s, outside it.
findings.reproduction: python3 probes/R5/probe_causality_available_ts.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-5-bundle $SCRATCH/mut/R5-validate/r2 (the second path is a copy of the rung-2-observe tools) -> 'sent 10.00: 3 of 7 keypoint entries and 3 of 7 frames arrived after the send; crop from a frame not yet arrived: True; missing tool=[] causal=[]' (1.46 s); 'sent 10.00: 4 of 7 ... missing tool=[] causal=['track', 'person_box', 'keypoints']' (1.60 s); 'part 2: den-observe demo wrote 6 observations with freshness.available_ts - capture_ts = [0.3] s; a bundle at the last capture ... holds 6 keypoint entries, 2 of them not yet available'; 'RESULT FAIL: 16 routed bundles (and the demo bundle) used observations that arrived after their send'
findings.suggested_fix: Add an open slot for the availability field (proposed freshness.available_ts). Admit an observation, and any track line naming it, only from its available time, and refuse scored runs until the slot closes. Add a gate check that no bundle entry arrived after its send.
findings.verification: 3 report(s) merged; 6 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: Lower to medium. The 1.46 s and 1.6 s cases set max_age_s 2.0. Rung 2's detector_max_age_s is open with a proposed 1.0 s, and older results become 'rejected:detector_result_expired', which rung 5's is_valid excludes. At that proposal the look-ahead is at most 1.0 s and the missing flags do not change (max_gap_s is 1.5). The '6.71 s / 10.71 s outside detection grace' arithmetic is outside rung 5: the ladder sets 'No latency threshold ... for bundles yet', and detection grace belongs to demand-gates. The documented capture-time rule is intended; what is missing is the slot or owner question. | Add one consequence: because the gate's verbatim clause (gate.py:100-107) wants every gated observation captured in the interval, it would also fail the bundles of a correct, causal live router (verify probe: 8 and 24 'left out' failures). The gate rewards non-causal replay bundles and rejects causal ones. The 6.71 s / 10.71 s versus grace comparison is the reporter's interpretation, but the arithmetic is right.
findings.rank_reason: other: replay bundles hold evidence not yet arrived

findings.title: Rung 3 judges a switch silent or reported at the first confidently labelled observation, so cannot-tell labels can flip the verdict either way.
findings.failure_scenario: truth.py drops '?' labels (truth.py:94-96), and switches() takes `confident` from the record holding the new person's first labelled observation. The owner labels about 1 s of a touching crossing 'cannot tell', the tracker reports ambiguity during the swap, and the interval settles (settle_s 0.75) before the first labelled frame. The switch is then scored silent and the gate fails wrongly. In the other direction, a swap made while confident and labelled '?' is scored as reported if the track turns ambiguous by the next labelled frame. That direction reproduced only on constructed records; it was 0 of 5 on real tracker output.
findings.reproduction: python3 scratchpad/probes/R3/probe_r3a_unsure_launders_swap.py <checkout>. Part 1: 'silent_swaps=0 reported=2 silent_swaps_zero=True' (FAIL). Part 2: 'silent_swaps=2 reported=0' (FAIL). Part 4, real tracker on synthetic touching/near/close crossings, seeds 200-219: 'reported switches 22; scored SILENT after "?" ... 12; "?" run lengths (s): [0.75, 0.77, 0.99, ...]', median 1.00 s.
findings.suggested_fix: Judge a switch over every scored record of that track between the last labelled observation of the old person and the first of the new one. Call it silent if any record there was confident and not covered by an ambiguous interval naming the other track; mark it unresolved otherwise.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: The mechanism is real, and a conservative blind labeller can trigger it: a +-1 s '?' span flipped 1 of 80 hard takes. One flip is enough to fail the 0-silent gate. But the 12-of-22 rate is an upper bound from a '?' span fitted to the tracker's ambiguous tail, not a realistic rate. With tight overlap-based '?' labels I saw no flips. The reproduced direction is a false NOT MET (reported scored as silent). The direction that gives a wrong PASS was not reproduced on tracker output, by the reporter or by me. Hence medium, not high. | The '12 of 22' figure uses a '?' span defined from the switch to the track's first confident record. Placing it needs the tracker's output, which a blind labeller does not have. Under labelling that follows image overlap, the effect is zero. It appears only when the labeller stays unsure about 1 s or more after the bodies separate. On real tracker output the direction is fail-safe (a false FAIL); the false-PASS direction appears only on constructed records. Downgrade to medium. It still matters because one spurious silent swap fails the whole gate, and the truth format gives no guidance on how long to mark '?'.
findings.rank_reason: wrong verdict: unsure labels flip silent and reported switches

findings.title: Nothing freezes rung 7's fit or held-out readings between scores, so blanking a failing reading turns fail into pass and the new score does not say it was dropped.
findings.failure_scenario: score_root re-reads every worksheet.csv and re-chooses the fit on each run (photometry.py:579-612; card.select, card.py:375 and 398). After score-1 prints a sofa point OUT (-16.4 lx at a 10 lx tolerance), the owner blanks that row as a 'bad reading', and score-2 prints PASS, listing the point only as 'nothing typed'. In a second case the owner blanks the day-1 fit row, so the next counter-1 capture of day 1, which score-1 excluded as 'repeats the fit', becomes the fit. k_L moves from 0.100 to 0.1089, every held-out point falls inside tolerance, and the gate passes. In a third case new_day accepts any date (photometry.py:181, exposed as the hidden --date at line 695) and never checks it against existing days or the capture times. A day-20261101 folder made after a failed score becomes day 1, and the fit moves to it. Held-out results thus leak into the fit, and the selection of held-out points, without detection.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/R7/probe_posthoc_heldout_edit.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-7-photometry -> 'A score-1: gate=fail ... (20261110-4, -16.37, False)' then 'A score-2: gate=pass ... unused=[(20261110-4, nothing typed)]'; 'B score-1: gate=fail fit=(20261110-1, 0.1) ... (20261110-4, -10.73, False), (20261111-1, -11.09, False)' then 'B score-2: gate=pass fit=(20261110-2, 0.108862)'; 'C: day folders now [day-20261101, day-20261110, day-20261111]; fit 20261110-1 -> 20261101-1'; 'RESULT FAIL (3 of 3 post-hoc changes went through silently)'

A later score lists every row or point that changed or disappeared since the first score and refuses (or marks not admitted). Refuse a new day dated at or before an existing day, or a capture whose time is not on its folder's date.
findings.verification: 1 report(s) merged; 2 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: The title says all three edits turn FAIL into PASS. Only A and B do in the probe; C moves the fit, but the gate stayed FAIL. C also needs the hidden --date flag (argparse.SUPPRESS, photometry.py:695) or a wrong PC clock, so the owner will not hit it by following the README. 'No trace' is overstated: score-1\report.json stays on disk with the failing point, and score-2's NOT USED list names the dropped capture ('nothing typed' / 'a card box only'). What is missing is any flag in the new score or its records that a reading which scored OUT, or the fit's own reading, was removed or changed. A consumer of the latest RoomModel sees only 'measured'. | "With no trace" is overstated. The score-1 folder, with the OUT point, is kept. Score-2 lists the blanked capture as 'nothing typed'. findings.title: Rung 7 now files a kept capture whose record cannot be read as interrupted, and the refusal blames its worksheet row, so deleting the row drops the capture and can turn fail into pass.
findings.failure_scenario: Day 2's desk capture is kept and its typed reading is 20 lx off, so score 1 FAILS on that held-out point. Later its capture.json can no longer be parsed, while the file itself, its frames, frames.jsonl and its worksheet row are all still there. Causes include a re-save by PowerShell 5.1 (Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 adds a BOM), a cut-off write from a disk or sync fault, or another program holding the file open. read_json turns OSError, ValueError (BOM, bad UTF-8, cut-off JSON) and a non-object into the same Refused. Since 29f0695f, score_root catches that Refused and files the folder as 'no capture.json (interrupted)' (photometry.py:601-605). METHOD-V1.md:236-238 skips only void captures and folders left without capture.json. The score then refuses with 'day-20261111\worksheet.csv has a row for capture 1, which is not a kept capture', which points at the row, not at the file. If the owner deletes the row, as the message implies, the next score prints RUNG 7 GATE: PASS on 3 held-out points, with the failing one gone. The console has no line about that capture: summarise never prints skipped_folders, although README step 9 says the score lists every capture it did not use. report.json says the folder had no capture.json. findings.title: Rung 8 Stage 1 scoring never compares the method it uses with the one the session recorded, so a session can be re-scored under edited numbers.
findings.failure_scenario: session.json records method_sha256 and method_stage1_block_sha256 when the session starts. run_session reads session.json (696) but only compares the Stage 0 meter-norm hash (702-704). Suppose that, after seeing session 1's FAIL, someone edits a scoring number in METHOD (noise_floor_multiple, min_unmasked_share, signal_rich_fraction, bracket_tolerance_multiple or block_px), deletes the three outputs and runs model.py again on the same session. It rescores the same hold-outs and may pass, with no refusal or flag. Only the new hash written into score.json and light-model.json differs from session.json's. That is tuning on hold-outs, which the ladder forbids.
findings.reproduction: Code evidence: model.py:691-712. run_session loads record = session.json and checks record['outcome'], the existing outputs and record['stage0']['meter_norm_sha256'] only. Its only uses of method1.file_sha256 and block_sha256 are writing them (709, 724-725). Scenario: session.json method_sha256 = A; METHOD edited to sha B; model.py --session writes score.json with method_sha256 = B and a verdict, and nothing compares A with B.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse to score when the scoring METHOD's file and block sha256 differ from session.json's, unless the session is explicitly moved to development and labelled not a gate result.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier

Medium stands, since the hashes in score.json versus session.json give an auditor a trail. | The finding was filed as plausible. It is now confirmed by a run. findings.title: One disturbed all-off capture can silently remove most rung 8 hold-outs, and the verdict is scored on what is left with no minimum and no count.

A model that is 30% wrong on hold-outs 1 to 12 goes from fail (median 22.0%) to pass (median 3.2%, p90 8.6%), scored on random_9 to random_12 only (576 of 2304 pairs).

The code follows METHOD-V1.md:385-388 and 438 ('a flagged value is not used'), which sets no minimum, so this is a design gap in method and code together. | 'No count' overstates it. score.json does carry error.count and per-hold-out pair counts in information_only.steps[].pairs. findings.title: Held-out scoring for the need test accepts an uncommitted, late-committed or edited gate file, so one edit can turn insufficient into feasible with no warning in the summary.
findings.failure_scenario: parse_gate (line 128) only refuses a fixed value that is null. run() (line 1053) only runs check_slots, which checks the slots, not the fixed values. gate_commit (line 173) records commit and dirty but nothing refuses on them, and nothing compares the commit time with the held-out asked_unix, which the run already has. Suppose the development step fills the slots and leaves a fixed value edited in the same block, such as interval.level 0.5 or sample.units/sessions/days 1. Or the held-out run is given an uncommitted gate through --gate. Then score.py --split held_out returns feasible where the canonical numbers give insufficient. The report carries gate.commit null, and the RESULTS.md line shows only the gate's sha256. A second held-out run after editing the gate is also accepted: nothing marks the held-out set as opened. This breaks GATE-V1's 'never slots' and 'after that it never changes', and plan section 7.3.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/N2/probe_gate-fixed-values-and-order-unenforced.py $SCRATCH/wt/den-n2 -> 'RESULT A canonical fixed values: verdict=insufficient reasons=[rule 2..., sample gate units.fine unmet]'; 'RESULT A edited fixed sample.* = 1: verdict=feasible gate.commit=None dirty=None'; 'RESULT B interval.level 0.95: verdict=insufficient competence.fine=[0.891119, 1.0] straddled'; 'RESULT B interval.level 0.5: verdict=feasible competence.fine=[0.957603, 1.0] met'; 'FAIL C: a gate that was never committed still gets a held-out verdict (gate.commit=None); held-out runs in this world: 2'. The only fixed-value test (test_den_n2.py:126) checks 3 of the 26 fixed keys, and only in the committed file.
findings.suggested_fix: Make FIXED_KEYS constants in score.py and refuse a gate whose fixed values differ. In held_out, refuse unless the gate is committed and clean and its commit_unix precedes the earliest held-out asked_unix. Put commit and dirty in the RESULTS line.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes:
The behaviour is real, but I rate it medium, not high.
- The plan's rule-1 refusal list (PLAN 4.7) does not include a dirty gate, a late commit or edited fixed values. GATE-V1.md and PLAN 7.3 say the commit time 'shows' the order, which describes an audit trail rather than a check the tool runs.
- A wrong verdict needs someone to edit a value that the gate's own prose calls 'never a slot'. Any edit changes the recorded gate sha256.
- What makes it worth fixing: the tool already computes dirty and commit_unix but never refuses on them. The EvalRecord stays on the PC, and the git-side RESULTS line has neither field. So an accidental dirty or late-committed gate leaves no trace in git.

Two parts of the scenario need correcting:
- gate.commit is null only for a gate outside git. In the documented flow (tools/den-n2/GATE-V1.md in the worktree), the report carries the last commit and dirty=True, and the verdict still flips.
- Scoring held-out more than once is partly intended: PLAN 7.5 rescores after an insufficient verdict, under a new labels version. What is missing is a block on rescoring the same labels version. | Downgrade high to medium. Arguments against: (1) the plan (section 7.3) and GATE-V1 make the git commit time the evidence of order ('its commit time ... shows the order'). The plan's rule-1 refusal list (section 4.7) does not include gate commit, dirty state or fixed values. The spec README requires a refusal only while a slot is open. (2) A wrong verdict needs someo
findings.rank_reason: wrong verdict: an edited or uncommitted gate is scored without warning

findings.title: The need test never checks that the replies were consumed, so a dead log scores not feasible with a misleading diagnosis and uses up the held-out set.
findings.failure_scenario: Suppose the yet-unbuilt n2_asks adapter or need v1 drops every facts event. For example, den-core's la-fact-log reader silently drops a line whose keys or source_id differ (sources._fact returns None). The replay then holds no inputs and passes check.py, because the replay drops them the same way. read_log() reads only person_state events, so the empty or all-'none' log scores every interval as missed and every unit as abstained. Verdict: not_feasible, diagnosis engagement [onset, early_off] and demand [competence.*, fine_recall, coverage], with unclear_share 0.0, while service shows 1416/1416 valid replies. Under the ladder this means: keep den_lighting, do not start the perception rungs, and the held-out set is used up.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/N2/attack/probe_dead_log_not_feasible.py $SCRATCH/wt/den-n2 -> 'RESULT [header only] verdict=not_feasible replied=1416/1416 rows={seen: 1416} diagnosis={engagement: [onset, early_off], demand: [competence.fine, competence.casual, fine_recall, coverage], cases: [...], unclear_share: 0.0}' and the same for a log with one 'none' record; 'FAIL ... scores not_feasible with no refusal or warning'.
findings.suggested_fix: Count the log's adapter input events per segment and refuse when they do not match the replied and no_box ask lines. Also refuse, or treat as insufficient, a segment whose need output never leaves none while it has valid seen rows.
findings.verification: 1 report(s) merged; 3 verifier vote(s), 1 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: The header-only variant cannot reach a verdict through the real den-core check.py. runner.run raises 'no inputs' (den-core runner.py:53-55), and check() does not catch it (check.py:34), so score.py would stop with a traceback. The example 'la-fact-log reader silently drops a line' is wrong. den-core sources.fact_log raises ValueError on any bad line except a torn last one (sources.py:82-87). An adapter that drops every input produces no log, which score.py refuses ('no replay log'). The realistic path is a log whose facts inputs need ignores (need never leaves none). That log replays identically, and the scorer then gives not_feasible without refusing, as reproduced. Downgraded to medium. Faults in need code or config would show at the development step, because held-out pins

findings.title: The need test measures fine recall per second and coverage pooled across bands, where the ladder defines recall per episode and coverage per band.
findings.failure_scenario: Ladder rung 6, whose gate re-runs N2's frozen gate on production need, gates 'fine-demand recall per episode (abstaining or stale counts as a miss) ... and per-band coverage'. The canon EvalRecord has coverage_per_band. score.py gates a per-second rate (lines 701 and 782), so long caught episodes outweigh short missed ones. It also gates one coverage averaged over fine and casual units together (line 784). With a 0.6 floor, a session where half the fine episodes are missed passes fine recall (0.90), and a casual band with coverage 0 passes the pooled coverage (0.60). No per-episode recall is reported anywhere.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/N2/probe_fine-recall-per-second-not-per-episode.py $SCRATCH/wt/den-n2 -> 'RESULT score.py fine_recall (per second) = 0.900; per episode = 0.500' / 'RESULT score.py coverage (pooled) = 0.600; per band = {fine: 1.0, casual: 0.0}'. Also probe_stats_recompute.py: per second 35/77 = 0.455 against per episode 2/3 = 0.667.
findings.suggested_fix: Report and gate fine recall per episode (a unit is a hit when its band is fine; abstained or stale counts as a miss), with the per-second rate kept as a diagnostic. Report and floor coverage per band.
findings.verification: 1 report(s) merged; 3 verifier vote(s), 1 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes:
Only the per-band coverage half changes the verdict. With the pooled coverage, a casual band at 0.29 coverage passes a 0.6 floor and the verdict is feasible, and the owner never sees per-band coverage because the report omits it. The per-episode recall half does not produce a wrong verdict. competence.fine is per unit and counts abstained or stale as a miss, and it can never exceed per-episode fine recall, so the reporter's 'half the fine episodes missed' scenario still ends not_feasible or insufficient. Its 'casual coverage 0' example is likewise caught, because abstained casual units make competence.casual 0. N2's own ladder gate names neither per-episode recall nor per-band coverage. The per-band requirement comes from the canon EvalRecord, rung 6 and E3. The plan (PLAN.md 4.4) documents the per-second and pooled definitions. | The finding's own examples do not change the verdict. Half the fine episodes missed is caught by competence.fine, which counts per unit and can never exceed per-episode recall. A casual band at coverage 0 is caught by competence.casual, because an abstained unit counts as wrong. What does produce a wrong feasible verdict:
(a) Casual levels that are right when fresh but mostly stale, which is realistic when hold rows ('unclear') keep a level in force. Pooled coverage 0.625 passes a 0.6 floor while casual coverage is 0.25, nothing else catches it, and neither report shows per-band coverage, so the owner cannot see or floor it.
(b) Per-episode fine mis
findings.rank_reason: wrong verdict: a starved band can pass pooled coverage

findings.title: The need test plan scores zero onset delay for any on-run begun in the unscored gap between tasks, so an estimator blind to touches passes the onset gate.
findings.failure_scenario: Section 4.2 (lines 204-214) gives d_on = 0 (entered_on) whenever the state at the touch is on and its on-run began after the previous labelled offset. It sets no limit on how early that run began. The gaps before 15/20 (hard-a) and 14/20 (hard-b) onsets lie wholly inside the previous task's tau_off (lines 221-224), and tau_off is left out of every measure (lines 184-186). So false_on, early_off and the quiet units never see what the estimator does there. Take an estimator that, after each task, emits one `ending` and then re-enters `engaged` on a single noisy reply (hold rows from hidden hands then keep it engaged, line 377), and never reacts to the next touch. It gets median onset 0 s, false_on 0, early_off 0, and every engagement unit right. A real responder at 6 s fails the 3 s gate. The plan's argument for scoring `stayed_on` as a miss (lines 221-230) is defeated by one `ending` record. The same zeros also pull D_dev down, so the pacing rule in 1(a) reports that onset fits at P = 4 s.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/N2plan/probe_entered-on-gap-flicker.py $SCRATCH/wt/plan-n2 -> 'RESULT hard-a honest6 : median onset 6.0 s (fails <= 3 s)'; 'RESULT hard-a flicker : median onset 0.0 s (passes <= 3 s); tags {'entered': 5, 'entered_on': 15}; false_on 0.000; early_off 0.000; entered_on runs began 23.5 to 43.5 s before the touch'; hard-b flicker gives median 0.0 with 14 entered_on; 'FAIL: a log that never reacts to 15/20 (hard-a) and 14/20 (hard-b) touches passes the onset gate ...'. Running it with the den-n2 checkout as root also prints 'den-n2 score.onset_of on the same log: median 0.0 s' (score.py:542-553 implements the plan rule).
findings.suggested_fix: Count entered_on as d_on = 0 only if the on-run began within one request period (P) or tau_on before the touch. Treat an earlier run like stayed_on (a miss), or score false_on in the short gaps. Report the lead time of every entered_on onset.
findings.verification: 1 report(s) merged; 2 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: The reporter's log is adversarial: it flickers only in short gaps and never in the scored quiet tails. A noisy estimator that also flickered in the 90 s tails would raise false_on. The onset defect holds either way, and my probe shows a single gap reply is enough. Onset tags are reported in `excluded`, so this is not fully silent. High is kept. | Severity lowered from high to medium. The failure is a gap in the gate design, and it follows A13's max(d_on, 0). A realistic flip needs many spurious on-runs that last to the touch in the unscored gaps while the scored quiet tails stay mostly off, so it is not a likely wrong verdict. The suggested fix (count entered_on as 0 only when the lead is within P or tau_on) needs no new owner number, so the plan's argument against a share cap (line 226) does not apply to it.
findings.rank_reason: wrong verdict: a touch-blind estimator passes the onset gate

findings.title: Rung 7 owner steps run captures with the incumbent active and lights set by hand, against the probe rule that it be paused and its normal scene restored.
findings.failure_scenario: Ladder rung 7 'tested' requires den_lighting paused, every probe logged as a non-human change and kept out of corrections, the saved normal scene written back from a pre-probe snapshot before den_lighting.resume_automatic, and a run that aborts on the occupancy gate or any change it did not send. README step 5 (lines 146-149) says 'den_lighting keeps running as usual'. METHOD-V1.md:96 says the tool never pauses or resumes den_lighting. Yet the capture line and step 8 have the owner set bulb scenes per illuminant class ('front left and front right at full', 'daylight only, no bulbs'). The incumbent routes any change it did not send to policy.manual(e, scene, now) with update_normal=True (den_lighting __init__.py:228-241, policy.py:87-95). So each photometry scene replaces the household's saved normal scene and is recorded as a human correction, and the next arrival restores the photometry scene. The capture also has no occupancy-gate or light-state check: a still person in view, or a change made between the meter reading and the hold, goes undetected unless it trips the hold1/hold3 region-mean repeat check.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/R7/probe_readme_probe_rule_den_lighting.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-7-photometry $SCRATCH/wt/den-core/ha-config/custom_components/den_lighting (policy.py copied to a temp dir) -> 'README+METHOD mention of pre-probe snapshot: 0', 'resume_automatic: 0', 'occupancy gate abort: 0', 'non-human / excluded from corrections: 0', 'README says den_lighting keeps running: True', 'light.den_front_left: normal before session=Scene(on=True, brightness=120, kelvin=2700) ; restored on next arrival=Scene(on=True, brightness=254, kelvin=4000)', 'FAIL ...'; exit 1
findings.suggested_fix: Document (or reuse rung 8 Stage 1's guard/probe tooling for) pausing den_lighting, snapshotting its saved normal scene, logging photometry light changes as non-human, writing the snapshot back before resume_automatic, and aborting a capture on occupancy or on any light change it did not request.
findings.verification: 1 report(s) merged; 2 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: The README never literally says 'set the lights'. Step 5 says 'Leave on whatever light you are measuring', and the --light examples ('front left and front right at full', 'daylight only, no bulbs') are logs of what is on. A manual change follows anyway: while den_lighting runs it puts its normal scene on at arrival, and no lux input exists ([[R17]]), so the README's own daylight-only class needs the owner to switch the bulbs off by hand. Severity lowered to medium: rung 7's verdicts and data are not affected, and no owner step fails. The harm is a contract deviation with household side effects: den_lighting learns the photometry scene as its normal scene, and the photometry changes enter the correction stream. The sub-claim about a still person or a mid-capture light change is weak, because the meter before/after drift check, the hold1/hold3 repeat check and the invariance check catch most such changes. | The tool itself sends no light command; the harm comes from the README's procedure. The sub-claim that a light change between the meter reading and the hold goes undetected is weaker than stated: the before/after meter drift check (meter_drift_max_percent 5, card.py:296-313) also catches a change that lasts until E_after is read. The probe simulates the owner's hand change through den_lighting's Controller.manual, which is what __init__.py routes external changes to; no live Home Assistant was involved. High is kept, because the README contradicts an explicit rung 7 protocol
findings.rank_reason: hardware: captures run with the incumbent active

findings.title: The rung 9 light-model adapter refuses the light model rung 8 Stage 1 actually writes, and its documented one-call swap understates the work, so no scored rung 9 run can use the real model.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner runs run.py --light-model <Stage 1's light-model.json> (the step the README describes for when Stage 1 lands; claude/rung-8-stage1 028981bc now exists). light_model.check() looks up dimming and basis by entity id (light.den_front_left). Stage 1 keys them by channel_key ('den_front_left.white', 'den_front_left.white@2202K') and writes None for excluded blocks, which _b() would also fail on. run.py exits 1. score.py refuses the fake, so no scored run can happen on rung 8's real model. The only 'real' model den-core accepts is its own format with the self-declared fake key removed (light_model.py:95), which is exactly what test_rung9.real_model() does to the invented numbers. Both arms go through den-core's reimplementation; den-light's predict() is never called.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/R9/probe_v_stage1_light_model_rejected.py $SCRATCH/wt/den-core-live $SCRATCH/wt/rung-8-stage1 -> 'RESULT stage1 basis keys look like [den_front_left.white@2202K, ...]; dimming keys [den_front_left.white, ...]' / 'FAIL den-core light_model.LightModel(stage-1 light-model.json) raised ValueError: not a light model: KeyError('light.den_front_left')' / 'FAIL run.py --light-model <stage-1 file>: exit 1 run.py: not a light model: KeyError('light.den_front_left')'
findings.suggested_fix: Have LightModel call den-light's predict() (via scene_from_ha) on Stage 1's channels/cct/basis_keys format and handle None points. Mark a model as a fake by where it came from (record/contract/sessions), not by an optional key.
findings.verification: 3 report(s) merged; 6 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: Downgrade from high to medium. The gate is not impossible by construction: it is blocked until a documented adapter swap, and the failure is loud. What remains: score.py:83-84's refusal text sends the owner to a step that fails today, and README.md:148-150's 'nothing else changes' understates the work. The integration also needs check()/describe(), per-bulb contribution() (Stage 1's predict() returns totals), handling of None for excluded blocks, and task_points slot values on Stage 1's 'r<row>c<col>' ids. Drop the fake-key point as a realistic failure path. | Severity should be medium, not high. The failure is loud (exit 1, 'not a light model') and never gives a wrong verdict. light_model.py:3-19 and README lines 144-150 say the adapter is a stand-in until Stage 1 lands, so the swap itself was expected. What remains a defect: den-core built and tested the adapter against its own entity-keyed reading of the plan, not against a fixture written from schemas.json's per-channel LightModel, which the spec README requires. So the swap is not the 'nothing else changes' one-call change the README promises: check(), _basis and contribution(entity_id) all assume entity keys, and Stage 1's predict() returns only totals. The sub-claim that a model is marked fake only by an optional key has no concrete failure path: no tool writes a den-core-format model without fake: true, so it takes a hand edit or the test helper.
findings.rank_reason: blocks owner: rung 9 scored run impossible on rung 8's real model

findings.title: The rung 10 verifier cannot read rung 8 Stage 1's light model (basis keyed by channel and temperature, a different call shape), so every decision comes out not verified.
findings.failure_scenario: Rung 8 Stage 1 (claude/rung-8-stage1 @028981bc, tools/den-light/model.py light_model() and predict.py) writes basis keyed '<channel_key>@<K>K', a cct map, dimming {levels, g}, and channels[{channel_key, entity_id}]. Its predict(scene, model) takes {channel_key: {level, cct_k}} and returns {'surfaces': {...}}. den-verify sets self.channels = set(data['basis']), so the channels become the '...@2202K' keys, and _scene() raises KeyError for any Decision channel. The owner's real model therefore yields 'decisions verified 0 of 1; hit rate None (0 of 0) ... insufficient' whether Decisions use channel_key or HA entity ids. The gate cannot pass by construction. The backend string still says 'Stage 1 not built'. The docstring's advice (swap _backend_predict and keep the {u, k} argument shape) would not work either: the channel check, the scene shape and the return shape all differ.
findings.reproduction: python3 probes/R10/probe_stage1-model-unreadable.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-10-verify $SCRATCH/wt/rung-8-stage1 -> 'RESULT rung 8 Stage 1 predict() on this model: {r00c00: 50.0, r00c01: 55.0, unit: relative}'; 'RESULT keyed by channel_key: exit 0; decisions verified 0 of 1; hit rate None (0 of 0), gate 0.85: insufficient'; not_verified reason 'light model lm-den-s1 has no basis for den_front_left.white' (same for light.den_front_left)
findings.suggested_fix: Re-implement predict() from the light_model record as Stage 1 serialises it (channels/cct/dimming{levels,g}/basis '<key>@<K>K', entity_id -> channel_key map) with a fixture written in that shape, and test against it.
findings.verification: 4 report(s) merged; 8 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: It fails closed: 0 verified and verdict 'insufficient', never a wrong pass. The backend is labelled a stand-in (light_model.py:1-7, BACKEND string), but the documented swap path is wrong. Add to the finding: the reader also fails on the canon light_model example's own basis shape, and that path raises an uncaught ValueError. | Downgraded from high to medium. This is a seam mismatch the consumer misreads, and it fails closed and loudly rather than making the gate wrong. The real remaining defect is that the documented swap path (light_model.py:6-7) understates the work: the channel set, the scene shape and the return shape all need re-implementing against Stage 1's record.
findings.rank_reason: blocks owner: rung 10 verifies nothing with the real model

findings.title: No tool produces the detector rows a scored rung 2 run needs, with completion times on the take's clock, and rows on the wall clock are refused.
findings.failure_scenario: A scored run needs host_monotonic rows whose capture_ts equals the take's t_host exactly (replay.py:69), at 640x360, with available_ts on that same Jetson clock (replay.py:138, detections.py:79). perception-lab's normalized box and pose results carry no completion time (from_perception_lab's own docstring). Live-loop events use Unix observed_at, which replay.py:64 refuses for a take. An offline detector pass over a take produces completion times on another machine, long after capture, so age_s would either expire everything or have to be invented. As built, the freshness half of the gate cannot be measured against R5's live 1.46 s baseline from data the plan collects, and no tool writes den-detections-1 rows with a real available_ts.
findings.reproduction: Evidence: detections.py:30-34 ('the caller supplies the frame's capture time, and the completion time if it has one, which those results do not carry'); perception-lab ultralytics_worker.py normalize_result (quality {}, no times); replay.py:64-65 refuses unix rows; replay.py:69-70 requires exact t_host equality; replay.py:138-139 requires available_ts for --scored.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the producer and its clock before the run. For example, record the live loop's per-bundle (rgb_seq, host capture time, completion time) beside the take, or convert Unix ledger times through the take's slate offset.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: 'No source can' goes too far. The specialist chain's frame bundle has frame_id, capture_epoch and available_at from the store clock (staged_specialist.py:147-150), so a producer could be built. The real defect is that none is built or specified, and the README describes a path that does not exist. The failure is a loud refusal (exit 2) of the scored run, not a wrong verdict. Status stays plausible: it rests on file:line evidence, with no runtime reproduction. | The title overstates. Rows with real completion times are not impossible by construction. A detector-side logger could stamp capture_ts from the bundle's own host-monotonic value (frames.csv stores t_host_s with repr, take.py:209, so exact equality is reachable). It could also map Unix completion times through the take's slate offset, which the tool already computes. The real defect: the branch neither builds nor names that producer and its clock mapping, the README implies it already exists, and replay refuses the format's own unix clock. There is no false verdict, because --scored refuses loudly without available_ts. Medium is kept only because the owner's detector windows are scarce (R5): an evening recorded without such a logger leaves nothing the freshness half of the gate can score. It is close to low.
findings.rank_reason: blocks owner: no way to produce rows a scored run accepts

findings.title: No tool writes the blind per-observation identity labels rung 3 scores against, and the rung named as their writer labels per track.
findings.failure_scenario: The README and truth.py say 'Rung 4's two-person labeller is meant to write' den-track-truth/v1: a person for every observation, labelled before seeing any tracker output. Ladder rung 4 ('A two-person gold set, per track') takes `track` as input and marks demand, worked patches and posture per track. It is not blind to tracker output by construction and writes no per-observation identity. Step 4 of the staged session therefore has no tool, and hand-writing labels for thousands of observations across 30 takes is not practical for the owner, so the gate cannot be run as described.
findings.reproduction: Evidence: tools/den-track/README.md step 4 ('the owner labels every person observation ... A, B, none or cannot tell') and truth.py:29-30. Ladder rung 4: 'in': ['track'], name 'A two-person gold set, per track', tested '... The owner marks, per track: when someone starts and stops working; the worked patch ...'. No branch writes den-track-truth/v1.
findings.suggested_fix: Name or build a blind per-observation identity labeller (for example a den-label extension reading observations.jsonl, not tracks), or define E2's truth per window (who is where before and after) so the owner can mark it by hand.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes:
A stronger argument than the finding gives: by the ladder, rung 4 is unblocked by rung 3's gate. Relying on rung 4's labeller for rung 3's truth is therefore circular, not just a format mismatch.

Mitigation the finding misses: unlabelled observations are not scored (pipeline.py:124-128), so the owner could label only the window frames. That shrinks the volume but still needs a tool, and README step 4 says to label every observation. | The line is README.md:96, not :81. Step 4 is README.md:128-131. The sub-claim 'not blind to tracker output by construction' goes too far: ladder rung 4 says its sessions are 'labelled blind'. What holds is that rung 4's marks are keyed per track (in: track) and cover demand, worked patch and posture, not identity per observation, so rung 4 as specified will not produce den-track-truth/v1.
findings.rank_reason: blocks owner: no tool writes the blind identity labels

findings.title: A rung 10 run with two evenings crashes on frame ids that carry no date, so the session bootstrap interval the owner chose is never produced.
findings.failure_scenario: The interval is computed over the local days inside a single run, so it needs at least two days in one run. LightStates carry no id (den-photometry writes none), so den-verify names them ls-HHMMSS[.hh] in local time with no date, and Run() raises ValueError on a duplicate (score.py:206-207). Frames on whole seconds from two evenings collide at once. Jittered frames every ~3 s over two 3 h evenings give 10 collisions. In both cases the CLI dies with a traceback and writes nothing. A den_lighting that saw the HA entity become unavailable went unknown -> on, which is not an arrival, and sent no ON for that bulb. run.py's gap report (lines 266-270) only covers spans that start at an 'on', so it prints nothing here.
