findings.title: A person's dimmer or switch change within 8 s after an incumbent command is filed as the incumbent's own report and never counted as a correction.
findings.failure_scenario: On arrival den_lighting turns a bulb on with a 2 s transition. A dims it with a Hue dimmer, which writes an id-less 'on' row that does not flip the bulb on or off. (a) A dims 3.5 s later. This is inside den_lighting's phase: the hold is provisional, and read-back finds DIM instead of WARM, so the hold stays. (b) A dims 6.5 s later. This is after den_lighting's transition+3 s phase and its read-back, so den_lighting opens a manual hold at once, without provisional_fixtures. Both are human actions that opened a hold. _own_fade sets aside every id-less, non-flipping row from 2 s before to 8 s after any command (ACK_BEFORE_S/ACK_AFTER_S, line 37). attribute() then returns 'den_lighting' and capture() files the hold as own_fade_report. Neither touch is counted. In case (b) den_lighting's own judgement, a hold opened with no provisional phase, is in the status export but is ignored. These quick reactions to den_lighting's own changes are the corrections aimed most directly at the incumbent, so the people count is biased low. The README's Limits section does not list this.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/R0corr/probe_dimmer_after_command_not_counted.py $SCRATCH/wt/correction-capture -> 'FAIL: a) 3.5 s, provisional then confirmed -- people counted 0 (expected 1); not_counted [('opened', 'own_fade_report', None), ('confirmed', 'own_fade_report', 'den_lighting')]', 'FAIL: b) 6.5 s, den_lighting opens a manual hold -- people counted 0 (expected 1); not_counted [('opened', 'own_fade_report', 'den_lighting')]', 'PASS: c) 9.5 s, control -- people counted 1'. den_lighting's phase is in ha-config/custom_components/den_lighting/__init__.py:229-240 (id-less report -> provisional only while _readback or the _own record with transition+3 is live, else policy.manual).
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the id-less acknowledgement exemption only to holds den_lighting marked provisional, since a hold it opened directly is its own verdict of a touch. Report read-back-confirmed holds after a fade in their own source bucket instead of dropping them, and list the limit in the README.

The suggested fix (exempt only provisional holds) would count those echoes as people. The discriminator the tool already reads but does not use: the held target vs den_lighting's command target. A late echo carries the commanded target; a dimmer touch carries another level. findings.title: The rung 3 identity score uses a separate mapping per window and only in-window observations, unlike the standard whole-take score, and the method does not say so.
findings.failure_scenario: score_take calls id_counts per window, and pool sums the counts. Standard IDF1 uses one optimal mapping per sequence. A take with two windows and a reported swap between them scores IDF1 1.0 where one mapping gives 0.5. Fragments and ID errors outside windows never count, so a tracker that fragments outside the marked windows still meets IDF1 >= 0.9.
findings.reproduction: python3 scratchpad/probes/R3/probe_r3a_idf1_window_mapping.py <checkout>. Cases A and B (single window) match: 0.500 and 0.750. Case C: tool 1.000 vs independent 0.500. Case D: 1.000 vs 0.750. Case E: 1.000 vs 0.625. 'RESULT IDF1: FAIL ... in 3 of 5 cases'.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute IDF1 with one optimal mapping per take over all labelled observations (window-restricted figures can be reported beside it), and pool by summing the per-take counts.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 5 verifier vote(s), 1 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes:
In case C the swap sits at the start of window 2, so the switch itself is still counted there as reported. Only IDF1 misses it. With the planned one window per take, the practical gap is case E: fragmentation and ID errors outside windows never count. | Keep this finding, but at low severity, and narrow it.

(a) The general claim 'so it exceeds take-level IDF1' is false for the documented one-window-per-take script: realistic sessions split about 50/50, and verdict flips go both ways. A window-scoped IDF1 is a defensible reading of a ladder gate stated per crossing.

(b) 'ID errors outside windows never count' is wrong for switches. scorer_core.py:79-86 counts switches outside windows, and pool() at :101 and :106 fails the gate on a silent one. Only fragmentation, and the persistence of a reported swap, go unscored outside windows.

(c) The real residual defect is the per-window mapping inside multi-window takes, which the truth format and the tool's own tests support. A reported swap that persists into a later window of the same take loses its IDF1 penalty: case C gives 1.0 against 0.5 under one mapping, and the gate passes.

The owner-facing METHOD.md does not state the scope. Fix: either reject or flag takes with more than one window, or use one mapping per take across all of its windows, and state the IDF1 scope in METHOD.md.
findings.rank_reason: other: nonstandard metric not stated in the method

findings.title: Rung 8 Stage 1 scoring can leave readings, a passing light model and a cut-off score on disk while printing that nothing was written, for example when all-off noise is exactly zero.

If a block's all-off frames repeat exactly, its noise is 0 and e/noise becomes inf (516); a static dark den under ISP temporal denoise can do this. A step's median_snr is then inf, and json.dump raises ValueError halfway through score.json. main catches ValueError and prints 'Refused: ... Nothing was written.' with exit 2 (740-742). On disk: readings.json, a light-model.json whose error block says verdict 'pass', and a score.json that is not valid JSON. Agents read light-model.json, so they see a pass. Running the same command again refuses with 'readings.json already exists', and the owner has to delete files by hand. Any ValueError or OSError from fit() or the writes leaves files behind in the same way.

Nothing was written.'; files: ['readings.json', 'light-model.json', 'score.json']; all-off spreads max 0.0; score.json is NOT valid JSON (1186 bytes, ends '"median_snr": '); light-model.json error {'median_pct': 2.3065, 'p90_pct': 11.3624, 'verdict': 'pass'}; attempt 2: 'Refused: readings.json already exists. Nothing was written.'; 2 FAIL
findings.suggested_fix: Floor the noise (or write SNR as null when noise is 0), build all three records in memory, write each to a temp file and rename, and say exactly which files exist when it stops.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: The 'pass' in light-model.json is the correctly computed gate verdict. Only the information-only median_snr fails to serialize, so this is misleading failure handling, not a wrong verdict. The inf needs more than half of a hold-out's scored blocks to have exactly zero all-off spread (an all-off crushed to black). That is plausible in a dark den at the held exposure but not shown on the real camera. A plain rerun after deleting the files hits the same inf, so the session cannot be scored without a code change. The general claim holds by construction: any exception after line 711 leaves files behind while the message says 'Nothing was written'. Medium stands. | Small precision fix: line 516 does not compute e/0. It takes an explicit float('inf') branch when noise[b] == 0. Exactly zero all-off spread needs the block's sampled pixels to be identical across the settled frames, which is plausible for black all-off frames at the short held exposure after dark. findings.title: The dispersion estimate keeps corrections from zero-hour blocks in its fitted rate but drops those blocks from its residual sum.
findings.failure_scenario: phi_hat sums stratum totals over every per_session entry (lines 250-253) but computes the Pearson sum only over sessions with occupied_h > 0 (line 254). A session with corrections but 0.0 rounded hours keeps its count in the fitted rate, so observed and fitted totals disagree. Example: (1 h, 1), (1 h, 1), (0 h, 2) gives 1.0, where the GLM fit gives 0.0. Real data reach this only when a counted action gets no exposure after it in its block and stratum, such as a last-row action or one right before a restart.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/R0corr/probe_phi_recompute.py $SCRATCH/wt/correction-capture -> 'FAIL zero-hour session with corrections tool=1.0 irls_by_stratum=0.0 irls_intercept_only=0.0'; all other cases PASS
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the stratum totals over the same sessions used in the Pearson sum (occupied_h > 0), and report how many sessions were dropped.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: The failure condition is narrower than 'no exposure after it'. The session also needs no exposure before the hold in that block and stratum. So the hold's status row must be the first in-charge row there: the previous row is not in charge, or is in the other stratum, or the hold comes just after the 20:00 UTC boundary. That row must also be followed by no exposure: it is the export's last row, or the next row is a restart. A plain hold followed by a restart, with in-charge rows before it, does not trigger it. | The trigger is narrower than 'a counted action gets no exposure after it'. The whole block and stratum must have zero in-charge exposure. That needs one status row that both starts the in-charge time (occupancy on, automatic on, or a stratum change) and shows the new hold, followed by a restart or the export's end. The other way is under 0.18 s of exposure, which rounds to 0.0 h. A last-row action in an evening that already had in-charge time does not trigger it (variant c). Side observation, outside this finding: in variant c the 30 s partial block with 1 correction drives phi_hat to 74.57. That is correct by the formula, but it shows short partial blocks at the export's end can dominate phi_hat.
findings.rank_reason: other: dispersion estimate slightly off in rare cases

findings.title: The planned hours per arm multiply by an unfloored dispersion estimate, so an under-dispersed sample plans fewer hours than the dispersion-free case, down to zero.
findings.failure_scenario: With a handful of evenings, counts proportional to hours (2 h/1, 4 h/2, 6 h/3) give phi_hat 0.0, and the record then says a 30% improvement needs 0.0 occupied hours per arm (Poisson: 296 h). More generally, any phi_hat < 1 from a few blocks scales the planning hours below the Poisson minimum.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/R0corr/probe_phi_hat_zero_gives_zero_hours.py $SCRATCH/wt/correction-capture -> 'RESULT: phi_hat 0.0; people hours_per_arm 296.0 at phi 1; hours_per_arm_at_phi_hat 0.0', 'FAIL: planning hours at phi_hat (0.0) fall below the Poisson (phi 1) hours (296.0)'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use max(1, phi_hat) for planning hours and report the raw phi_hat beside it.
findings.verification: 1 report(s) merged; 2 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: phi_hat exactly 0 needs counts exactly proportional to hours, which is unrealistic. The realistic case is phi_hat somewhat below 1, which is common with few blocks (for example 0.9833 for plausible counts in my verify probe; with df = 3, chi2/df < 1 about 60% of the time). The figure then sits below the Poisson hours. Low is right: the field is reported only, never used by the verdict, and the raw phi_hat appears beside it.
findings.rank_reason: other: planning value below the dispersion-free minimum

findings.title: A rung 1 fit interrupted between its two appends leaves a resolvable camera entry with no calibration record, and the re-run supersedes a record that does not exist.

When the owner re-runs fit, the already_registered check (which reads calibrations only) misses it, and the tool registers .2, whose CalibrationRecord supersedes a calibration id that does not exist. Nothing reports the half-written registration.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/R1/probe_interrupted-fit-orphan.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-1-register -> 're-run: exit 0, registered den-oak@2027-01-15.2', 'room-model.jsonl revisions: 2; calibration records: 1; camera entries without a CalibrationRecord: ['cal-den-oak-pose-2027-01-15.1']', 'the re-run's CalibrationRecord supersedes 'cal-den-oak-pose-2027-01-15.1', which does not exist in calibration-records.jsonl', 'FAIL A'
findings.suggested_fix: Append the CalibrationRecord first and the RoomModel revision last (the revision is what makes the id resolvable), and refuse a fit while any camera entry's calibration_id has no record.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes:
Severity low holds. The orphan passed every gate before it was written, and its pose is byte-identical to the re-run's, so there is no wrong verdict and no wrong transform. The harm is a provenance gap (a resolvable camera entry with no CalibrationRecord, a dangling supersedes, no fit-N.json for the failed run) plus a traceback instead of a named refusal.

Trigger: a Ctrl+C landing in the microsecond window between the two appends is improbable. The realistic triggers are a sharing violation (a program that locks the file) or a crash/kill.

Add register.py:310 (the calibrations-only already_registered check) as a second anchor.

Suggested-fix caveat: reversing the append order alone would trade the orphan for an 'already_registered' refusal that names a transform_id that does not resolve, because the digest would be in calibrations while room-model lacks the entry. The consistency check (the suggestion's second half) is the part that matters. The failing fit should also end in a named refusal, not a traceback. | The failure scenario holds as stated. The process exit code in the interrupted run is 1 (Python's code for an uncaught exception), with no verdict line and no fit-N.json.

The suggested fix as written would make things worse. I simulated its order (CalibrationRecord first, crash before the RoomModel line). The re-run then refuses with 'already_registered: these inputs were registered as den-oak@2027-01-15.1', and that id resolves as transform_unknown (probe step4). Th
findings.rank_reason: other: half-written registration leaves a provenance gap

findings.title: Rung 1 resolve crashes with a traceback on a camera entry shaped like the schema's own example.
findings.failure_scenario: room-model.jsonl may be seeded with today's approximate placement as schemas.json shows it (den-oak@2026-10-18: pose is a string, error_bound_m is null). Then `register.py resolve C:\den-register den-oak@2026-10-18` crashes with a TypeError traceback instead of a named refusal, outside the README's documented exit codes 0, 1 and 2.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/R1/probe_interrupted-fit-orphan.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-1-register -> 'FAIL B: resolve den-oak@2026-10-18 on the schema's own example entry crashes: TypeError: string indices must be integers, not 'str''
findings.suggested_fix: In run_resolve, read the pose through records.room_from_camera (refuse transform_unknown if it is not numeric) and print 'error bound null' when error_bound_m is absent.
findings.verification: 1 report(s) merged; 2 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes:
Exit code: it is not outside 0/1/2. CPython exits 1 on the uncaught TypeError (observed 'CLI exit 1'). That is the same code resolve returns for INVALIDATED (register.py:552-555), and README.md:154-157 says 1 means 'refused ... with the reason printed and saved'. So a script or owner reading $LASTEXITCODE sees the crash as a refused/invalidated transform, while no reason reaches stdout (the traceback goes to stderr only).

Second crash site: register.py:550 also fails with a numeric pose whenever error_bound_m is null, which schemas.json documents as today's value. A fix needs to handle both lines.

Severity low holds: it is a read-only lookup, nothing is written, and no verdict is affected. | Two corrections:
- The exit code is not outside 0/1/2. The process exits 1 (Python's code for an uncaught exception). The README reads exit 1 as 'refused ... with the reason printed and saved in fit-N.json or mount-N.json', but nothing is printed on stdout and nothing is saved. The output misleads; the code is not a new value.
- The scenario should cite the tool's own test (test_den_register.py:466-485) as the source of the seeded state, not only a possible manual seeding.

On the suggested fix: refusing with transform_unknown for an entry that records.resolve finds, and that the schema says the transform_id resolves to, would contradict the test's line 485. Printing the entry's method and pose text with 'no numeric pose, error bound null' would be more faithful. Severity: keep low.
findings.rank_reason: other: traceback instead of refusal

findings.title: Rung 1 lets fit and check roles be swapped after a refused fit, and the passing calibration record shows no trace of the failed held-out check.
findings.failure_scenario: Check c1 is mismeasured by 7 cm, so fit-1 is REFUSED with check_over_gate. The owner edits worksheet.json to make c1 a fit point and p4 a check, then fits again: REGISTERED. c1's residual is 4.1 cm and LOO 9.1 cm. held_out lists p4 at 2.5 cm and c2 at 2.0 cm as passing independent checks. Nothing in the CalibrationRecord or the RoomModel entry refers to fit-1.json or the earlier roles. The worksheet hash changes, so already_registered does not fire. README Step 6 pins slots before any fit result, but nothing pins roles.
findings.reproduction: Same probe as checks-near-fit-points-pass, scenario B. It prints 'first fit: refused [check_over_gate]', 'after swapping c1 (fit) and p4 (check): registered den-oak@2027-01-15.1', 'held_out: {tolerance_m 0.05, result pass, points [p4 0.024893 pass, c2 0.019662 pass]}' and 'record mentions the refused first attempt: False; fit files [fit-1.json, fit-2.json]'.
findings.suggested_fix: Freeze roles at the first fit for a worksheet's set of marks, and refuse a later fit with different roles unless a new check mark is added. Alternatively, list every earlier attempt (fit-N hash, roles, verdict) in the CalibrationRecord inputs.
findings.verification: 1 report(s) merged; 2 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier

CHANGED needs a valid-depth occluder over more than half of the comparable cells: one person within about 0.5 m of the camera (still beyond the roughly 0.35 m stereo minimum) or three people abreast at 1.2 m. The README's 'too much of the view blocked -> UNKNOWN' is also wrong for blockers with no depth: UNKNOWN needs more than 75% of cells without depth, and at 80% of the width the tool answered UNCHANGED from 16 edge cells. A: 1 requests (1 no_box)'; 'CLI gate on that replay: exit 0, last line: verdict: pass (...)'

findings.title: The rung 5 per-person period counts tracks whose bundles have no box and are never sent.
findings.failure_scenario: per_person_period_s is computed as min_interval_s times len(tracks), where tracks are all tracks eligible at the start (router.py:137-138), including tracks whose bundles are no_box. A fix must change the rule text too: either count only tracks that could be sent at that tick, or record a measured period. The field is nominal in other ways as well (latency and back-off), and that should be stated whichever fix is chosen. | Severity stays low. The failure scenario overstates who would be misled: no consumer exists in this branch. The checkpoint's availability analysis has to use sent_ts/outcome anyway, because per_person_period_s is nominal and also differs from measured gaps under slow answers (13 s vs 8) and back-off (35.25 s vs 8). findings.title: Stage 0's exposure sweep cannot detect frame-adaptive global tone processing, so it says go for a camera that cannot add bulbs linearly.
findings.failure_scenario: An exposure sweep of a fixed scene scales every pixel's irradiance by the same factor, which is exactly a uniform change in scene brightness. Take an ISP whose global tone curve adapts to frame brightness (gain (mean/ref)^-a). It fits one curve perfectly, and every region agrees. Stage 0 passes: residual about 1 code, regions within 2.15%. Stage 1 then holds one exposure and switches bulbs, so the frame mean changes and the curve moves. Blocks dominated by one bulb are over-predicted by (M/m_c)^(a/(1-a)). With a=0.3 the four-bulb hold-out (all four at full) scores median 10.1%, p90 17.9%, failing the rung 8 gate after about 5 build days and a probe session. Stage 0 was meant to find this before Stage 1 is built. Session 1's planned 'one bulb at full at three of Stage 0's exposures' (PLAN.md:409-410) is also exposure-only and cannot catch it.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/R8s0/probe_adaptive-global-tone-passes-stage0.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-8-stage0 -> 'a=0.0: Stage 0 verdict PASS ... superposition ... median 0.3% p90 0.8% -> rung 8 gate met'; 'a=0.1: ... PASS ... median 2.3% p90 3.6%'; 'a=0.3: Stage 0 verdict PASS reasons [] residual {r: 1.11, g: 1.01, b: 1.09} region tested 48/48 worst deviation 2.15%'; 'a=0.3: superposition ... median 10.1% p90 17.9% -> rung 8 gate NOT met'; 'PASS (reproduced)'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a fixed-exposure superposition check to Stage 0 (A, B, A+B and off at one held exposure, with the owner switching a bulb), or state that Stage 0's GO covers exposure linearity only.
findings.verification: 1 report(s) merged; 2 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: The camera model is a pure power-law, frame-mean-adaptive gain, which is the case most favourable to the finding. A real adaptive tone curve that is not power-law would leave some residual. Nothing in the repo shows that the OAK ISP adapts its global curve while exposure and ISO are manual. That premise is unverified. The rung 8 gate in Stage 1 still catches the a=0.3 case, so there is no wrong final rung verdict. The cost is a false Stage 0 GO and the wasted Stage 1 build and probe session. Keep medium only on that basis. | Severity medium -> low. The 10.1%/17.9% figure covers one hold-out only: all four bulbs at full, the case with the largest change in frame mean. The gate scores the pooled 16 hold-outs (PLAN.md:450-463), so 'fails the rung 8 gate' is not shown, and a=0.1 passes it. Stage 1's own hold-out gate catches a camera that cannot superpose, so no wrong final verdict results. The cost is Stage 1 build effort plus one probe session. It is also unverified that the OAK ISP adapts a global tone curve while exposure, ISO and white balance are held manually. The proposed bulb-switching check would change Stage 0's approval scope ('The tool writes no lights'). The proportionate fix is to state that Stage 0's GO covers exposure linearity and spatial uniformity only.
findings.rank_reason: other: camera check misses a known failure mode

findings.title: Stage 0's residual is a per-frame, per-pixel figure with no noise reference, so a camera with one fixed tone curve can fail on sensor noise alone.
findings.failure_scenario: residual_rms compares F(X*E) with each frame's raw code, so it contains all per-pixel sensor noise, and frames_per_step frames are never averaged. Noise lives on the NV12 Y/U/V bytes; the BT.601 decode amplifies V into R by 1.6x and U into B by 2.0x. With sigma = 2 codes on Y/U/V and a camera with one static tone curve (no tone mapping), the residual is R 4.44 and B 4.98, above the proposed R = 4. Stage 0 says FAIL while the region test passes (2.2%). A no-go sends the owner to RAW output (a bigger camera change) or to stopping rung 8, for a camera that linearises fine. Noise added on decoded RGB instead: 2 codes passes (2.3), 3 codes passes (3.4), so the limit is close to realistic noise.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/R8s0/probe_region-test-noise-sensitivity.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-8-stage0 --yuv 2.0 -> 'RESULT noise=2.0 codes on NV12 Y/U/V: verdict FAIL reasons ['residual'] residual {'r': 4.44, 'g': 3.25, 'b': 4.98} worst region deviation 2.20% failing region-channels 0/48'. RGB-noise runs: noise 2.0 PASS residual 2.31/2.22/2.16; noise 3.0 PASS 3.37/3.25/3.14. METHOD-V1.md:62 (residual_max_codes = 4, open), meter.py:467-475.
findings.suggested_fix: Score the residual on per-step frame means, or normalise it by frame-to-frame noise measured from the kept frames, and set R relative to that noise per channel.
findings.verification: 1 report(s) merged; 2 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: Downgrade to low. The probe adds independent sigma=2 code noise to the U and V bytes of the 640x360 NV12 stream. That stream is an ISP downscale of the 1080p or sensor output (PLAN.md:72-73), so each output pixel and each 4:2:0 chroma sample averages several source pixels, and the ISP also denoises chroma. Two codes of U/V noise per sample there is unlikely. With Y noise of 2 and smaller chroma noise, the R residual is about 2.5 codes and passes. R is an open slot the owner must confirm before any run, and sweep.py refuses while it is open. The per-sample residual is the documented METHOD-V1 definition. What remains real is a design weakness: the residual mixes noise with misfit and has no noise reference. | The defect is real but depends on things not yet known. R is an open slot holding a proposed value, and sweep.py refuses to run until the owner confirms it (sweep.py:858-859, as the spec README requires). This is therefore a warning about a proposed number before it is confirmed, not a fixed gate. The failure needs about 1.7 to 2 codes of independent per-pixel noise on U and V as well as on Y. The 640x360 stream is downscaled and chroma-denoised by the ISP, where chroma noise is usually below luma noise. At sigma 1 the check passes, with R 2.35 and B 2.66. A FAIL on the residual alone, with the region test passing, is visible in response.json (check.residual.codes and check.region_test). The 3 kept frames per step let the noise be measured. Recovery still needs METHOD-V2
findings.rank_reason: other: camera check can fail a good camera

findings.title: A Stage 0 sweep killed during its minute-long fit writes no record, and recheck then refuses the complete data.
findings.failure_scenario: After 'Released. Fitting the response (under a minute)...', Ctrl+C is trapped, but closing the PowerShell window, Ctrl+Break (SIGBREAK is not handled), a crash or laptop sleep end the process before response.json exists. That happens at sweep.py:839, after meter.check at 820. The folder keeps all frames and frames.jsonl, released and complete. But --recheck needs response.json with outcome pass, fail or error (sweep.py:917-922), so it refuses. The complete sweep cannot be scored, and its frames are neither recorded nor deleted. The owner must use the camera again. The fit took 112 s here under load, and 40-75 s in other runs.
findings.reproduction: python3 -B probes/R8s0/probe_kill-during-fit-loses-record.py $SCRATCH/wt/rung-8-stage0 -> 'child said: ... Holding: 12 exposures. | Released. Fitting the response (under a minute)... | FITTING'; 'after the kill: sweep-1: released=True frames.jsonl lines=24 frame files=24 steps=[1]..[12] response.json exists=False'; '--recheck exit 2: Refused: no readable response.json in the sweep folder.'; 'PASS (reproduced)'.
findings.suggested_fix: Write response.json (outcome 'fitting', data complete, release result) atomically right after the release, update it after the fit, and let --recheck finish a 'fitting' or missing record from complete frames.
findings.verification: 2 report(s) merged; 4 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes: Downgrade to low. Laptop sleep suspends the process; it does not end it. An exception in the fit, which is the 'crash' case, is caught at sweep.py:828-830: the outcome is error, response.json is written and the frames are kept. Only a hard kill loses the record: closing the window, Ctrl+Break, or power loss, inside a window of about 30-60 s after the owner has been told to wait (README: 'fits for up to a minute'). The 40-112 s timings came from a loaded host. Frames and frames.jsonl stay intact and uncorrupted. The cost is one camera rerun, and approval 1 covers 3 reruns that evening. | Severity medium -> low. The plan, METHOD and README promise only that Ctrl+C and exceptions cannot lose the record (PLAN.md:193-199, METHOD-V1.md:174-180, README.md:206-209). A hard kill is therefore a hardening gap, not a broken promise. Laptop sleep suspends the process rather than ending it, so it is not a trigger. Python errors, MemoryError included, are caught at sweep.py:828 and recorded as outcome error. The realistic triggers are closing the window, Ctrl+Break, or power loss during a fit of about a minute that the owner was told to wait for. The frames stay on disk, complete. The cost is a folder the tool cannot score plus a one-minute rerun, with no wrong verdict and no lost or published frames.

findings.title: The need test plan never fixes which clock the replies' observed and valid-until times use.
findings.failure_scenario: The adapter puts each facts event at the take's started_unix in whole seconds + r + S (lines 390-392). The plan uses the only per-frame wall clock, recv_pc_unix, for the time label (line 420), but never says which clock the receipt's observed_at and valid_until use. The 'fresh' and 'stale on arrival' tests compare against valid_until (lines 175-176, 365). If a builder takes observed_at from recv_pc_unix, the two clocks differ by the first-frame delay plus the fraction of a second dropped from started_unix. The 10 s validity then stretches or shrinks by that much, so stale levels count as fresh hits, against the agreed rule that stale = miss.

2. The same gap covers generated_at and first_receipt's now/available_at. If those take the GPU host's wall clock at ask time (days later), any "stale on arrival" test read against the receipt's own available_at marks every reply stale. That failure is loud, not silent.

findings.title: The split alternates in registration order, not in recording order (started_unix) as PROTOCOL-V1 states
findings.failure_scenario: The owner records hard-a take X, then hard-a take Y a day later, but runs check.py and 'sessions' on Y first. Y gets order 1 (development) and X order 2 (held_out), the reverse of the stated rule. When check.py is run decides which recording is held out, and remark_take(), which sorts by started_unix, can name a different session than the registration order implies.
findings.reproduction: Same probe as copied-take: 'hard-a entries (order, split, started_unix): {a_late: (1, development, 1793188800.0), a_early: (2, held_out, 1793102400.0)}' and 'INFO hard-a recorded first is assigned second'. PROTOCOL-V1.md Split: 'sessions alternate ... in recording order (take.json's started_unix)'.
findings.suggested_fix: Either refuse to register a take whose started_unix precedes an already-registered take of the same script, or state the rule as registration order in PROTOCOL-V1 before the okay.
findings.verification: 1 report; 3 verifier vote(s), 1 refuting; reproduced by an independent verifier
findings.verifier_notes:
This is not leakage: no held-out content is exposed and the split is still fixed before any pass. It is protocol text that disagrees with the code. The behaviour is deliberate: SplitTests.test_stable_when_sessions_are_added_and_never_reassigns (test_den_label.py:334-339) asserts that a0, recorded earlier but registered later, continues the alternation. PROTOCOL-V1.md:131-133 ('Sessions added later continue the same alternation') partly covers this case. The real defect is that the 'in recording order (started_unix)' sentence is false whenever takes are registered out of order. remark_take() sorting by started_unix matches the protocol's re-mark rule, so that part is not a defect. The trigger needs a take whose check passes only after a later take of the same script was registered (for example check-1 FAIL, a later re-check PASS). That is not the normal README step-5 flow. No gate is affected: with at most two takes a day, the held-out set still spans 2 or more days. | Not leakage. Splits are fixed at registration, before any pass, without looking at content, and N2 uses split.json as written. The real, small and loud consequences:
(a) PROTOCOL-V1's 'recording order' and 'the first of each script is development' are false after a late registration. Fix the text before approval 1, for example: 'in registration order; within one sessions run, by started_unix'.
(b) A registration-order split combined with a recording-order re-mark pick can move the re-mark target off a session al

findings.title: The staged-take steps never tell A to reopen the slate page for the end slate after using the phone during the take.
findings.failure_scenario: hard-a and hard-b each have 5 'Use your phone at the counter.' blocks. By the end slate at 1,500 s, the phone is on another app or the browser has dropped the background tab. Step 8 only says 'The slates are as in Step 6', and Step 6 assumes the slate page is still on screen. N1's plan says 'At the end slate, open the slate page again', but the README the owner follows leaves this out. If A used Step 3's fallback (the page served from the PC, then the server stopped with Ctrl+C), a dropped tab cannot even be reloaded. Three unreadable end attempts mean A_end_slate FAIL, and a 27-minute staged take is lost.
findings.reproduction: File and line evidence: den-take-script tools/den-take/README.md:145-164 (Step 8: line 151 'Keep your phone in a pocket between its blocks', line 157 'The slates are as in Step 6.'), README.md:68-77 (the fallback server is stopped once the page loads), scripts/hard-a.json lines 9, 17, 25, 34 and 42 (phone_at_counter blocks), plan-n1 docs/plans/n1-reference/PLAN.md:324-326 ('At the end slate, open the slate page again.'). grep finds no such instruction in tools/den-take/README.md or tools/den-label/README.md.
findings.suggested_fix: In Step 8, and in the spoken end 'Hold the phone' cue for staged scripts, add: reopen slate.html, tap for full screen, turn brightness up. Recommend the copied-file route over the stopped-server fallback for staged takes.
findings.verification: 1 report(s) merged; 2 verifier vote(s), 0 refuting; argued from file:line, not reproduced by a verifier
findings.verifier_notes: Downgrade from medium to low. A note on the suggested fix: slate.html:36-41 registers its tap handler with {once: true}. After switching apps, a second tap does not request full screen or the wake lock again, so 'tap for full screen' works only after a reload, and a reload is impossible under the stopped-server fallback. The pattern keeps drawing either way (requestAnimationFrame resumes), so the slate can still be read without full screen. | Lowered to low. take.py:427-442 gives the end slate 3 attempts over about 71 s (5 s lead, 3 x 20 s, 2 x 3 s gaps), each with 'Unreadable, again.' A also used the same page for the start slate minutes earlier. If the slate still fails, check.py correctly FAILs the take: the frames are kept, no verdict is wrong, and the cost is one re-take. The strongest case is the Step 3 fallback (server stopped) combined with a background tab the browser has dropped. slate.html:39-40 also needs a tap to get full screen and the wake lock back after switching apps.
